note: Recent arXiv papers, broken down from their abstracts. Each entry says what the authors claim, not more. status is the authors' own comment line. New entries are added by the daily digest job; the newest are first.

papers.t: On the potential of widening the band of X-ray polarimetry
papers.by: Nicolas De Angelis
papers.status: 17 pages, 2 figures, PoS paper from the Multifrequency Behaviour of High Energy Cosmic Sources - XV (MULTIF2025) workshop, https://pos.sissa.it/506/069/. Published in PoS(MULTIF2025)069
papers.one: We then summarise how these techniques are being implemented, or could be, in REDSoX and GOSoX, eXTP, XPP, WXPT and in EXPO and PHEMTO, proposed to the ESA M8 call, as well as in the wide-field transient polarimeter POLAR-2, and…
papers.q: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has made X-ray polarimetry a routine astrophysical diagnostic, but its sensitivity is confined to the 2-8 keV band, where the photoelectric effect in a gas is most efficiently exploited. Several of the questions raised by its results, as well as some classical goals of high-energy astrophysics, require polarimetry below 2~keV, to reach the thermal emission of neutron stars, black-hole discs and blazars, and above 8~keV, where reflection, cyclotron lines and the non-thermal emission of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae and magnetars can be isolated.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: Following a recent review of the subject, we discuss the scientific case for extending the band over roughly 0.1-80 keV and beyond, and the techniques that can deliver it: Bragg diffraction on graded multilayers, photoelectric gas imagers read out by pixel ASICs with time-of-arrival capability, time projection chambers and focal-plane Compton polarimeters, including their combination in stacked focal planes.

papers.t: Euclid: Discovery of a quasar at z = 8.13 hosting a 360-million-solar-mass black hole
papers.by: J. Wolf, S. Belladitta, D. Yang and 57 others
papers.status: Published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, Volume 715, Article A356 on November 24, 2026. Published in Astron. Astrophys. 715, A356 (2026)
papers.one: Conversely, previously known reionisation-era quasars may represent the rapidly accreting end of a broader population of already massive black holes spanning a wider range of accretion states.
papers.q: Quasars powered by rapid accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have been uncovered deep into the first gigayear of cosmic history. J1504+6252 exhibits the defining spectral signatures of archetypal quasars at lower redshift, including a luminous blue power-law continuum and broad permitted emission lines, indicating a classical broad-line region.
papers.how: We present the discovery of EUCL J150452.291+625224.39 (J1504+6252), selected from Euclid Wide Survey imaging and spectroscopically confirmed as the first quasar at z > 8 through observations with Keck, HST, LBT, and JWST.
found: JWST/NIRSpec G395M spectroscopy yields a systemic redshift of z = 8.129 +/- 0.005, corresponding to 630 Myr after the Big Bang and shifting the quasar redshift frontier by about 39 Myr (6% of the age of the Universe at that epoch).
From H-beta and Mg II, we measured intrinsic broad-line-region FWHM of 3160 +/- 270 and 3740 (+160/-170) km/s, respectively.

papers.t: The Jupiter ICy moons Explorer (JUICE) Mission: Post-Launch Status and Mission Overview
papers.by: Olivier Witasse, Giuseppe Sarri, Christian Erd and 57 others
papers.status: 47 pages, 14 figures. Published in Space Science Reviews (2026) 222:85
papers.one: The payload includes 10 instruments and one experiment using the spacecraft's telecommunications system to connect with ground-based radio telescopes, plus an onboard radiation monitor.
papers.q: The JUpiter ICy Moons Explorer (JUICE) is the first large-class mission in ESA's Cosmic Vision programme. Proposed in 2007 and selected in 2012, it was launched on 14 April 2023 from Kourou and is now en route towards Jupiter.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: After arrival in July 2031, JUICE will spend approximately four years studying the Jupiter system, performing multiple flybys of three of its Galilean moons, the icy moons Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto, before entering orbit around Ganymede for its final year.

JUICE will also conduct a global investigation of the Jupiter system as the archetype for gaseous giant planet systems: it will study Jupiter's atmospheric circulation, composition, and flow of energy from the cloud tops to the thermosphere and characterise the 3D structure of the magnetosphere and its coupling with the ionosphere and thermosphere.

papers.t: Two-Component Model for the Unidentified Extended Fermi-LAT Source 4FGL J1908.6+0915e / FL16Y J1908.6+0915e in the SGR 1900+14--W49A Sky Region
papers.by: Vadym Voitsekhovskyi, Roman Hnatyk, Bohdan Hnatyk and 4 others
papers.status: NN pages, 10 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in Galaxies
papers.one: However, due to the considerable distance to the magnetar (d=12.5 kpc), the required cosmic-ray energy budget in both hadronic and leptonic scenarios corresponds to a hypernova explosion and/or a powerful magnetar wind nebula created by a newly born millisecond magnetar…
papers.q: Galactic PeVatrons are expected to be powerful sources of non-thermal high-energy (HE, E>100 MeV) and very-high-energy (VHE, E>100 GeV) γ-ray emission as a manifestation of acceleration processes in supernova remnants (SNRs), star formation regions (SFRs), and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe). In the sky region containing the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the young massive star cluster (YMSC) W49A, there is one recently identified point-like source FL16Y J1910.2+0903, and there are three unidentified gamma-ray sources: the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e, the HAWC extended source 4HWC J1908+0845, and the LHAASO point-like source LHAASO J1907+0913.
papers.how: We investigate the possibility of explaining the HE and VHE γ-ray emission from the SGR 1900+14--W49A sky region using a model of the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e as superposition of two extended sources -- a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the stellar-wind superbubble adjacent to the YMSC W49A complex. To this end, we simulate the observed γ-ray emission in hadronic and leptonic models using the open NAIMA code and show that it consists of two extended regions: the stellar wind superbubble in W49A region -- an analog of the Westerlund 1 superbubble -- powered by the YMSC W49A (the southern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e); and the SGR 1900+14 region, powered by a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar (the northern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e).

papers.t: Blowing star formation away in AGN Hosts (BAH) - VI. Warm Molecular Outflows Driven by the Low-Luminosity AGN in NGC 3884
papers.by: José Henrique Costa-Souza, Rogemar A. Riffel, Nadia L. Zakamska and 5 others
papers.status: Accepted for publication by AAS
papers.one: By decomposing the emission-line profiles into multiple Gaussian components, we detect both ionized and warm molecular outflows, traced by [Ar ii] 6.99 um and H2 0-0 S(5), respectively.
papers.q: The ionized and warm molecular components both extend to similar distances from the nucleus, reaching approximately ~1.2 kpc. In addition to an outflow component, we detect a double narrow emission component in both ionized and molecular lines, clearly observed along the minor axis with similar amplitudes, while their intensity ratio varies systematically along the major axis.
papers.how: We use the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrograph (MRS) to investigate the warm molecular and low ionization gas outflows driven by the low-luminosity Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) in NGC 3884.
found: We estimate that the outflow injects momentum into the interstellar medium (ISM) at a rate corresponding to ~0.015 percent of the AGN bolometric luminosity, consistent with a radiation-driven origin.
Assuming a constant outflow rate, the gas reservoir would be depleted on a timescale of ~26 Myr, potentially suppressing nuclear star formation in the host galaxy.

papers.t: Updated View on Titan's Habitability: Interior and Surface Aqueous Environments
papers.by: Diogo Gonçalves, Lígia F. Coelho, Catarina Miranda and Zita Martins
papers.status: 45 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Manuscript published in Front. Astron. Space Sci. Published in Front. Astron. Space Sci. (2026) 13:1916097
papers.one: For each setting, we identify the enabling factors and the principal bottlenecks that limit prebiotic complexification.
papers.q: Saturn's moon Titan is the only world beyond Earth where abundant organic molecules and liquid water are expected to interact. Crucially, these interactions yield prebiotic molecules central to terrestrial biochemistry.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.

papers.t: Probing for relativistic outflows in the Ultraluminous X-ray pulsar RX J0209.6-7427
papers.by: F. Barra, C. Pinto, T. di Salvo and 2 others
papers.status: 14 pages, 14 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.one: If associated with outflows, the inferred column densities appear lower than those reported for some persistent ULXs, potentially reflecting differences in the accretion-flow properties or the shorter super-Eddington phase of RX J0209.6-7427.
papers.q: Relativistic winds have been observed in Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs), but their detection at large distances remains limited. Galactic neutron stars accreting matter from Be-star companions provide a valuable opportunity to improve our understanding of these outflows.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: RX J0209.6-7427 is a Be-XRB, powered by a neutron star with a spin period of 9.3 seconds, that underwent an outburst in 2019, exceeding a bolometric luminosity of 10³⁹ erg s⁻¹ at its peak.
The RGS spectrum yields 105,000 counts, a factor of two higher than any other deep ULX RGS spectrum.

papers.t: An ALMA Survey of Molecular Gas in the Host Galaxies of Fast Radio Bursts
papers.by: Bunyo Hatsukade, Tetsuya Hashimoto, Yuu Niino and 4 others
papers.status: Accepted for publication in PASJ
papers.one: These results allow a compact persistent-source contribution and a possible spectral turnover between centimeter and millimeter wavelengths, although the present sensitivity and resolution prevent a firm separation from surrounding star-forming emission.
papers.q: CO emission is significantly detected in 6 hosts and tentatively detected in one, yielding molecular gas masses of 2.2x10^8-1.0x10^10 Mo for a Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor. All 6 detections show spatially resolved emission and large-scale velocity gradients, several consistent with ordered disk rotation.
papers.how: We present ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission and millimeter continuum measurements for 9 localized fast radio burst (FRB) hosts at z=0.05-0.38.
found: At the position of the repeating FRB20201124A, the measured 98 GHz continuum flux density is above the predicted star-formation contribution and lies at the lower end of or below an extrapolation of the VLA spectrum.

papers.t: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
papers.by: Emir Tataroglu, Jonathan C. Tan, Rosalia D. O'Brien and Devesh Nandal
papers.status: Submitted to ApJ, comments welcome
papers.one: Latest CIB observations place constraints of λ_Edd ≲ 0.3 for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.
papers.q: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Lyα radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium.
papers.how: We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al.
found: (2026), our fiducial model assumes ~10⁵ M☉ Pop III.1 stars forming by z_flash=20 with a comoving number density of ~0.2 cMpc⁻³.
For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than 1% of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements.

papers.t: First Ωₘ-w Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.by: Yi-Ying Wang, Shi-Jie Gao, Chi Zhang and Yi-Zhong Fan
papers.status: 8 pages, 5 figures. Table I of the Supplemental Material lists 169 localized FRBs
papers.one: Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density Ωₘ and dark energy equation of state parameter w from FRBs alone…
papers.q: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid Ωₘ-w constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth.
papers.how: We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at 0.105 ≤ z ≤ 2.148, we obtain Ωₘ = 0.33^+0.10_-0.11 and w = -0.80^+0.28_-0.38 under the flat wCDM model.

papers.t: Demographic inference in exoplanet chemistry is shaped by retrieval assumptions
papers.by: Dwaipayan Dubey, Karan Molaverdikhani, Barbara Ercolano and 3 others
papers.status: 52 Figures, 10 Tables, Accepted in Communications Chemistry
papers.one: Our results suggest that population-level chemical trends inferred from free-chemistry retrievals should be interpreted with caution unless sample selection, residual structure, prior sensitivity, and chemical assumptions are explicitly tested.
papers.q: Understanding the chemical diversity of exoplanet atmospheres is crucial for linking atmospheric composition to planetary formation history. Atmospheric C/O can provide clues about where and how planets form, particularly through the accretion of gas and solids across disk snowlines.
papers.how: We present atmospheric retrievals for 20 transiting planets with published JWST transmission spectra, including complementary HST spectra for targets where such data are available, spanning gas giants, warm Neptunes, and temperate/warm sub-Neptunes, to test how population-level chemical inferences depend on retrieval assumptions.
found: Several hot Jupiters converge to low C/O ( ≤ 0.05), whereas colder, cloudy planets retain broad posteriors that reflect limited information content of their spectra.

papers.t: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
papers.by: Hao-Tian Lan, Qin Wu, Jia-Wei Luo and 2 others
papers.status: Accepted for publication in ApJ; 8 figures, 1 table
papers.one: Robust periodicity searches must evaluate significance against null models that account for the observed waiting-time statistics and the full search procedure.
papers.q: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients with high brightness temperatures, but their physical origin remains uncertain. The association of FRB 200428 with a Galactic magnetar provides compelling evidence that at least some FRBs originate from magnetar-like systems.
papers.how: Motivated by the reported 1.7 s periodicity in the active repeater FRB 20201124A, we conduct a systematic search for short-timescale periodicity in four highly active repeating FRB sources.
found: The search yields apparent period candidates with nominal Poisson-calibrated significances comparable to that reported for the 1.7 s signal, although the inferred periods vary substantially among sources and observing windows.
We therefore find no robust evidence for a short intrinsic periodicity in these data, and the reported 1.7 s signal is not uniquely distinguished from clustering-induced candidates.

papers.t: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.by: Vishal Baibhav, Valerio De Luca, Loris Del Grosso and 3 others
papers.status: 14 pages, 5 figures
papers.one: We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the…
papers.q: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.

papers.t: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
papers.by: Lisa Kaltenegger, Abigail Bohl, Connor Novak and Gillis Lowry
papers.status: 9 pages, accepted ApJ
papers.one: Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.
papers.q: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology.
papers.how: Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV).

papers.t: A novel pathway to stellar-mass black hole growth: Re-accretion of gas from stellar wind bubbles
papers.by: D. Kománek, R. Wünsch, S. Martínez-González and 2 others
papers.status: Accepted for publication in A&A
papers.one: Conversely, we find no significant re-accretion in scenarios involving an SN explosion or high-metallicity progenitors; in these cases, fast winds or SN ejecta efficiently evacuate dense structures from the bubble interior, leaving behind a hot, low-density medium. [abridged] This mechanism…
papers.q: We investigate whether newly formed stellar-mass BHs in dense molecular clouds can significantly increase their final mass by accreting gas from pre-existing, wind-blown interstellar bubbles produced by their progenitor stars. We performed 1D and 3D hydrodynamic simulations of interstellar bubbles driven by stellar feedback, incorporating thermal conduction, radiative cooling, gravity, ionizing radiation, stellar winds, and supernova (SN) explosions.
papers.how: The formation of high-mass stellar black holes (BHs) observed in mergers by gravitational wave observatories remains difficult to explain using standard models of stellar evolution. Scenarios exhibiting significant re-accretion were further validated using high-resolution 3D simulations.
found: Our parameter space study encompasses over 500 1D simulations, varying initial cloud densities, gravitational binding energies, progenitor masses (40-257 M☉), and metallicities (0.66 Z☉ and 0.016 Z☉), and tracks the bubble evolution for millions of years post-BH formation.

Our simulations show that BHs formed via direct collapse from low-metallicity progenitors can accrete up to 6.9 M☉ of gas from massive inner shells formed by late-stage slow winds, resulting in final BH masses of up to 93 M☉.

papers.t: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
papers.by: Tasneem Basra Khan, Liton Majumdar, Mithun Patra and 4 others
papers.status: 28 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Revised and resubmitted to The Astronomical Journal. We thank the anonymous referee for their constructive comments. Further comments are welcome
papers.one: Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.
papers.q: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%.
papers.how: We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns).
found: For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03).

papers.t: Deconstructing the cosmic baryon distribution with fast radio bursts
papers.by: Koustav Konar, Yin-Zhe Ma, Léon V. E. Koopmans and P. Daniel Meerburg
papers.status: Accepted for publication in A&A
papers.one: Our bin-wise electron density estimate reproduces the simulation ground truth to within 10 per cent and gives gas fractions of 0.186 ±0.012, 0.179 ±0.015 and 0.046 ±0.014 in voids, filaments and haloes, against ground truths of 0.167…
papers.q: The precise distribution of baryons in the Universe remains an open question in cosmology, as their highly diffuse nature hinders direct observation. However, mapping it is integral for precision cosmology in studies of gravitational lensing, galaxy evolution and the cosmic microwave background with current and upcoming surveys.
papers.how: We use fast radio bursts (FRBs) and their dispersion measures (DMs) to probe and localise this baryon distribution in the large-scale structure (LSS). Using IllustrisTNG simulations, we classify the LSS into eight bins of increasing matter density, analogous to voids, filaments, and haloes.
found: Combining the FRB and galaxy density estimators, we recover the density of ionised baryons as Ω_b fᵢₒₙ = 0.0455^+0.0028_-0.0026 (simulation: 0.0462), corresponding to Ω_b = 0.0479^+0.0029_-0.0027 for fᵢₒₙ=0.95.

papers.t: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
papers.by: Chirag Chawla, Sourav Chatterjee and Katelyn Breivik
papers.status: 28 pages, 13 figures, 1 table, submitted to the Astrophysical Journal; comments welcome
papers.one: Interestingly, our models suggest that future releases will also include 22⁺⁷₋₅ (13⁺⁵₋₄) and 124⁺¹⁴₋₁₅ (53⁺¹⁰₋₆) gaiamock-detectable pulsar--MS binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively, for the rapid (delayed) model, which are prime targets for radio follow-up.
papers.q: With the fourth data release (DR4) from Gaia imminent, we predict neutron star (NS) binaries with luminous companions (LCs) expected to be detectable in DR4 and the final data release (DR5). Across supernova models and statistical fluctuations, the former (gaiamock) pipeline predicts ~14--29 (~1--8), 4500--4700 (100--110), and 4800--5000 (300--380) detectable NS--LC binaries in DR3, DR4, and DR5, respectively.
papers.how: We create realistic synthetic populations of NS--LC binaries in the Milky Way using COSMIC, assuming (a) observationally motivated initial distributions of binary properties, (b) metallicity and location dependent star formation history of the MW adopted from the FIRE-2 galaxy m12i, and (c) all relevant binary interaction physics, with the rapid and delayed supernova prescriptions. We estimate the detectable NS--LC population using an approximate Gaia\ selection function based on projected orbital size of the LC as well as gaiamock, which emulates Gaia's multi-epoch astrometry and orbit-fitting pipeline- both after taking into account extinction and reddening.
found: While the orbital-size based pipeline brackets the DR3 yield of NS--LC candidates, the gaiamock prediction falls short, suggesting uncertainties in the modeled binary evolution or contributions from other formation channels.
DR4 is expected to directly shed light on the the relative importance of detectable NS--LC binaries from isolated binary evolution vis a vis other channels such as dynamical formation.

papers.t: Exomoons and Exorings with the Habitable Worlds Observatory. III. Icy Moons and Rings Often Outshine Their Planets
papers.by: Sam Hopper, Mary Anne Limbach and Rachel Bowens-Rubin
papers.status: Accepted to AJ
papers.one: We find that reflected light from Triton-analog exomoons and Saturn-analog exorings is detectable with HWO over a broad parameter space.
papers.q: If we could observe the Solar System's giant planets with the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), the dominant sources of reflected near-infrared light would not always be the planets themselves. In fact, the brightest sources are split roughly evenly between the giants and their icy companions: at the locations of the giant planets, the dominant point sources would be Jupiter, Saturn's rings, Uranus, and Triton (Neptune's icy moon).
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: In the nearest systems, icy Titan-sized moons are detectable at star-moon separations of ~2 AU and icy Earth-sized moons out to ~6 AU.

Moreover, Saturn-like exorings are likely to be the brightest point sources in many extrasolar systems, capable of greatly outshining any planets, while remaining potentially detectable at system distances out to 100 pc.

papers.t: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
papers.by: Filippo Mannucci, Matteo Ceci, Norman A. Grogin and 11 others
papers.status: MCT Concept White Paper, Genesis initiative, comments are welcome
papers.one: The census will deliver pair fractions as functions of redshift, separation and luminosity, BH masses and mass ratios, host properties and environments, and the empirical anchor needed to turn merger models into realistic LISA rate forecasts.
papers.q: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: JWST has opened the window to study these systems at z>3.
Confirming and characterising about 100 pairs requires of order 1000 hr, well beyond the ceiling of standard TAC programs, and demands multi-cycle continuity.

papers.t: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.by: Alexander Salganik, Sergey S. Tsygankov, Roman Krivonos and 2 others
papers.status: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A
papers.one: IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.
papers.q: At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, E_cyc, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state.

We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at L₃₋₇₉ ≃ 5×10³⁶, 4×10³⁵, and 6×10³⁴ erg s⁻¹, respectively.

papers.t: The JWST Sub-Jupiters Survey: Observed Sensitivities to the Wide-Separation, Cold, Sub-Jupiter Exoplanet Population
papers.by: Giovanni M. Strampelli, Aarynn L. Carter, Beth Biller and 32 others
papers.status: 40 pages, 17 figures, 8 tables. Accepted for publication at AJ
papers.one: We find that these programs are sensitive to sub-Saturn to Jupiter mass exoplanets with effective temperature (Tₑff) as low as ≲ 250 K, already at ~2 arcsec.
papers.q: A comparison with the SHINE survey confirms that the improvements in mass sensitivity provided by JWST high-contrast imaging surveys outpace current ground observation for masses ≲ 1 M_J and separations between ~20-500 au, opening up a novel parameter space to explore. Overall, this analysis provides a robust framework for interpreting future exoplanet detections.
papers.how: We present a sensitivity analysis of three recent JWST direct imaging programs (GO-4050, GO-5835, and SURVEY-6005) designed to build a demographic study of sub-Jupiter mass ($0.1 - 1$ M_J) exoplanets in nearby young associations and moving groups.

papers.t: Unexpected Plateau: The Constant logε(Th/Eu) Ratio of Actinide-Boost Stars
papers.by: J. Shejeelammal, Asa Skuladottir, Marta Molero and 4 others
papers.status: Accepted for publication in A&A
papers.one: Combined with other evidence, our results suggest that mergers with neutron stars are the most promising astrophysical site for actinide-boost stars.
papers.q: The astrophysical site of the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) is still one of the major open questions in astronomy. A key mystery is the origin of the peculiar actinide-to-lanthanide ratio found in the so called actinide-boost stars, with logε(Th/Eu)>-0.35.
papers.how: Here we present the largest sample of Th measurements in stars formed in an external galaxy, Gaia Sausage Enceladus. From this sample, we present the three most metal-rich actinide-boost stars discovered to date, -1.6<[Fe/H]<-1.1.
found: Unexpectedly, actinide-boost stars lie on a very narrow (σ=0.02) plateau of logε(Th/Eu)=-0.2, clearly separated from actinide-normal stars.
Chemical evolution models show that such a plateau can arise, even at [Fe/H] = -1, when a single actinide-rich event dominates the r-process content of a small or gas-depleted system.

papers.t: The Velocity Curves and Three-Dimensional Kinematics of the Milky Way from Gaia DR3
papers.by: Petr Zavada and Karel Píška
papers.status: 19 pages, 17 figures, 4 tables. Published in Galaxies 2026, 14(6), 101
papers.one: To facilitate the description of the observations, we employ a simplified axisymmetric Monte Carlo model with several free parameters that reproduces the main kinematic trends.
papers.q: From these data, we determine the local solar velocity (U☉,V☉,W☉) = (10.5±0.7,14.5±0.9,7.33±0.1) ~km/s, the average rotation velocity\linebreak V₀ = (228±4) km/s, and the circular velocity V_c = (234±4) {km/s,} both at the radius R☉. Next, within the range of 3-14 kpc, we derive the Galactic circular velocity curve V_c(R) and determine the average spherical components of the stellar velocities as functions of both Galactocentric radius R and distance from the Galactic plane vertZvert.
papers.how: We investigate the fundamental kinematic parameters of stellar motions in the Milky Way using a statistical sample of 27,485,720 stars with measured three-dimensional velocities from the Gaia DR3 catalogue.
found: In particular, the pattern observed at R ≲ 5 kpc can be associated with the influence of the Galactic bar.

papers.t: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
papers.by: Xiao Li and En-Wei Liang
papers.status: 16 pages, 2 table, 13 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
papers.one: These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics.
papers.q: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. Identifying distinct burst populations and investigating their variations across active episodes provide important insights into the physical origins of repeating FRBs.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: In this paper, we apply an unsupervised machine learning approach to bursts from three active episodes of FRB 20121102A observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST).

Notably, Cluster 1 exhibits bimodal-like distributions in central frequency and bandwidth and contains nearly all high-energy bursts, with a mean energy about an order of magnitude higher than those of the other clusters.

papers.t: Receiving Exoplanet Messages with Gravitational-wave Carriers: The Gravitational-wave Radial Velocity Method
papers.by: Casey McGrath
papers.status: 21 pages, 7 figures. Published by The Astrophysical Journal. Published in Astrophysical Journal 1012 (2026) pp. 21
papers.one: In this work we show that while similar to electromagnetic-based RV, this GW-based method depends on the ''phase modulation index'' (PMI), a parameter that is more sensitive to high-mass, long-period exoplanets.
papers.q: Gravitational-wave (GW) radial velocity (RV) may offer a new method for detecting exoplanets, one that would primarily target planets orbiting GW-emitting, ultracompact, post-main-sequence stellar objects such as white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. We investigate the potential of GW RV for GW sources in both the mid-frequency spectrum (where the upcoming LISA mission will operate) and the high-frequency spectrum (where the current LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observatories operate).
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.
found: Remarkably, we find that the PMI increases by a factor of ~O(10⁴ - 10⁶) going from the mid-frequency to the high-frequency GW spectrum, which results in a greater redistribution of observed power due to the exoplanet's presence.

papers.t: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and ΛCDM simulations
papers.by: Mariana P. Júlio, Marcel S. Pawlowski and Noam I. Libeskind
papers.status: Accepted for publication in ApJ on 17-10-2026. 30 pages, 12 figures, 8 tables
papers.one: We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates.
papers.q: Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of ~53%, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues (~17-27%).
papers.how: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations.
found: This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut (M⋆> 10⁴ M☉) to match the resolution limits of the simulations.
In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of ~28%.

papers.t: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
papers.by: Changwen Zeng, Zhiwei Chen, Youjun Lu and 2 others
papers.status: 24 pages, 14 figures; accepted for publication in A&A
papers.one: For the 15 strictly constrained bursts, we find a median Eₖ ≃ 3.8×10⁴⁹ erg and η_γ ≃ 0.35, with respective 68% intervals of [5.1×10⁴⁸,1.9×10⁵⁰] erg and [0.09, 0.79].
papers.q: Short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs) are believed to originate from compact binary mergers, particularly binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, providing a probe of jet energetics and merger remnants. We derive distributions of beaming-corrected jet kinetic energy Eₖ and radiative efficiency η_γ, and combine these with binary population synthesis and numerical simulations to infer remnant black hole (BH) magnetic fields assuming the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) jet-launching mechanism.
papers.how: We compile broadband afterglow observations of 40 sGRBs and perform forward-shock modeling with off-axis Gaussian jets, excluding data potentially affected by additional energy injection.
found: The inferred magnetic field supplied by the accretion disk and threading the BH horizon is approximately 7×10¹⁵ G, with a 68% credible interval of [2.3×10¹⁵,2.4×10¹⁶] G, depending slightly on the neutron star equation of state.
The full sample yields a higher median field of approximately 2×10¹⁶ G, with the high-energy and high-field tails predominantly contributed by less well-constrained bursts.

papers.t: The Same But Different: SiO₂ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
papers.by: Joshua D. Lothringer, Jeff A. Valenti, Sarah E. Moran and 9 others
papers.status: 36 pages, 13 figures, 12 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ
papers.one: These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.
papers.q: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~μm spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5).
papers.how: Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO₂ clouds in both objects.
found: Our observations include spectral features from H₂O, CO, CO₂, CH₄, Na, and K and cover approximately 98% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects.
We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback.

papers.t: Stellar-Field-Driven Induction Heating Unlikely To Cause Significant Heating in Giant Exoplanets
papers.by: Madison Brady, Darryl Z. Seligman and Cassidy Walker
papers.status: 31 pages, 14 figures, accepted in MNRAS
papers.one: However, hot Jupiters with large wind speeds may have high magnetic Reynolds numbers and therefore be in the inductive regime.
papers.q: A planet moving through a changing magnetic field will have a current induced on it by that magnetic field. If the magnetic Reynolds number in the upper atmosphere of this planet is small, the dissipation of this current could result in observable changes to the planet's properties.
papers.how: The abstract does not describe the method in detail.

papers.t: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
papers.by: Rodrigo Ferrer-Chavez, Jason J. Wang, Katherine L. Bouman and 4 others
papers.status: Published in Nature
papers.one: A new way of subtracting a star's glare lets the Webb telescope see planets two to fifteen times fainter than before.
papers.q: To photograph a planet you must remove the light of its star, which is millions of times brighter. The usual method subtracts an image of a reference star, but the telescope flexes slightly between the two exposures and the leftover glare hides faint planets. Can that limit be beaten?
papers.how: They built a physical model of how starlight passes through the telescope and its coronagraph, with millions of adjustable numbers describing the instrument's tiny drifts, and let software tune all of them at once to match the data. They tested it on real Webb NIRCam observations.
found: 2 to 15 times better than standard techniques
the planet 51 Eridani b detected at 4.3 micrometres
papers.why: The authors say the same approach could work on ground telescopes, on the Roman Space Telescope and on the planned Habitable Worlds Observatory, and could relax how rigid those telescopes need to be. Stability is one of the most expensive requirements in building them.
papers.careful: The abstract reports results for one instrument. How well the method transfers to others is a stated hope, not yet a demonstration.

papers.t: Searching for Planets around Altair with JWST/NIRCam
papers.by: Tiffany Meshkat, Charles Beichman, Jorge Llop-Sayson and 13 others
papers.status: 14 pages, 4 figures. Published in AJ 172, 280 (2026)
papers.one: Webb looked for giant planets around the bright nearby star Altair and found none, which rules out anything bigger than Saturn beyond ten times the Earth–Sun distance.
papers.q: Altair is one of the nearest and youngest stars in our neighbourhood, and young planets still glow with the heat of their formation. Does it have giant planets, and is it a good target for future imaging?
papers.how: Two sets of Webb images taken with a coronagraph blocking the star, at wavelengths of 2.0 and 4.4 micrometres. A real planet moves across the sky with its star; a background star does not, so the second visit sorts one from the other.
found: 150 billionths of the star's brightness at 2 arcseconds (10 AU)
planets heavier than Jupiter beyond 5 AU, heavier than Saturn beyond 10 AU
several; none moved with Altair, and their colours match background stars
papers.why: A clean non-detection is useful. It tells planet-formation models what this kind of star does not make, and it certifies Altair as a clean reference star for the Roman Space Telescope's coronagraph.
papers.careful: The mass limits depend on models of how bright a young planet of a given mass should be. Planets closer than about 5 AU remain hidden in the star's glare.

papers.t: Planetary material is a major source of hydrogen in helium-atmosphere white dwarfs
papers.by: Paula Izquierdo, Andrew Swan, Christopher J. Manser and 36 others
papers.status: Accepted by MNRAS
papers.one: At least a fifth of a certain kind of dead star got some of its hydrogen by swallowing pieces of its own planetary system.
papers.q: Some white dwarfs have atmospheres of nearly pure helium, yet traces of hydrogen show up in them and increase with age. Does that hydrogen float up from inside the star, or does it arrive from outside, in water-bearing asteroids and comets?
papers.how: A simple model that allows both routes, compared with two independent samples of helium-atmosphere white dwarfs from the DESI and Sloan surveys, at temperatures between about 10,000 and 19,000 K.
found: White dwarfs that must have taken in planetary hydrogen
at least 22 ± 2% of those with detectable hydrogen
ices, water-bearing minerals or planetary atmospheres
papers.why: It means the remains of planetary systems are delivering water-rich material to dead stars routinely, not just in a few extreme cases. White dwarfs are the one place where the insides of rocky bodies from other systems can be chemically analysed.
papers.careful: 22% is a lower limit, and the model is deliberately simple.

papers.t: Unidentified Sources in the 4FGL-DR4 Fermi-LAT Catalog as Potential Dark Matter Satellites
papers.by: Fernando Valenciano, Miguel A. Sánchez-Conde and Jorge Martin Camalich
papers.status: 14 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables
papers.one: None of the 2,428 unexplained gamma-ray sources in the sky looks like a clump of dark matter, and that absence rules out some kinds of dark matter particle.
papers.q: If dark matter is made of WIMPs, pairs of them should occasionally annihilate into gamma rays. The Milky Way's halo should contain small dark clumps with no stars, which would appear as gamma-ray sources with nothing else there. Are any of the Fermi telescope's unidentified sources such clumps?
papers.how: They started from the 2,428 sources in Fermi's 14-year catalogue that match no known object, filtered out those that cannot be dark clumps (wrong spectrum, variable, extended in the wrong way), and analysed the spectra of the rest in detail.
found: within a factor of 2 to 3 of the benchmark 'thermal relic' annihilation rate at the lowest masses
thermal WIMPs lighter than about 50 GeV annihilating to bottom quarks
papers.why: This is an independent check on the limits from dwarf galaxies, using a population of objects that cannot be studied any other way.
papers.careful: The limits depend on predictions of how many dark clumps the halo holds and how bright they would be, which come from simulations.

papers.t: Accretion variability as a probe of black holes and their environments: Light curve signatures of a single hot spot
papers.by: I. Urso, C. Deffayet, A. Held and F. H. Vincent
papers.status: Submitted to A&A
papers.one: The flicker of gas near a black hole carries a fingerprint of how the hole bends light, and this paper works out what to look for.
papers.q: A bright clump of gas orbiting close to a black hole brightens and fades as it circles. How much of that flicker comes from the clump itself and how much from the warped spacetime its light crosses on the way to us?
papers.how: Simulated movies of a single flickering hot spot, with its light traced to a distant observer three ways: through flat space, around a non-rotating black hole and around a spinning one. They compared the brightness records and their frequency content.
found: reproduces the main features at moderate viewing angles
in how different parts of the image vary relative to one another, which encodes orientation and lensing
papers.why: The black hole at the centre of the Milky Way flares several times a day. Timing signatures like these are a way to test gravity there without resolving an image.
papers.careful: The abstract gives no numbers, and the authors say more work is needed to see whether the conclusions hold for realistic discs and not just one idealised spot.

papers.t: Spacetime contactability in Galactic civilization networks: Contact counts and percolation
papers.by: Kohji Tsumura
papers.status: 24 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to Acta Astronautica
papers.one: If civilisations come and go at different times, a galaxy could be full of one-way messages even though almost no one ever gets a reply.
papers.q: Estimates of how many civilisations we might hear usually assume they all exist at once. Signals travel at the speed of light and civilisations have lifetimes, so who can actually hear whom, and can a network of contact form?
papers.how: Mathematics, not observation. The author derives how many others a civilisation hears over its lifetime, and the threshold at which contacts link into a connected network, then applies it to a disc shaped like the Milky Way.
found: Average number heard over a lifetime
twice a single 'contactability' number, whatever the timing
drops from 4.51 when all exist at once to 1.32 when lifetimes are short compared with travel times
Upper bound from our silence so far
a civilisation at the Sun's position would hear at most 5.5 others on average
complete exchanges become rare once signals take longer than lifetimes
papers.why: It reframes the silence: hearing nothing back is expected even in a populated galaxy. It is also a nice application of one-way light time to a question people care about.
papers.careful: This is a model built on assumptions nobody can test yet, and the bound assumes an ideal complete survey. It has not been peer reviewed.

papers.t: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
papers.by: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux and 43 others
papers.status: 53 pages, 21 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to AJ
papers.one: Ten months of observations of the third known visitor from another star, from its approach to its departure.
papers.q: 3I/ATLAS formed around another star. As it passed through the Solar System, how did its colour, dust and gas change, and how does it compare with our own comets?
papers.how: Images and spectra from the Keck and Gemini telescopes on 28 occasions between July 2025 and May 2026, in visible and near-infrared light, covering the passage around the Sun.
found: did not change significantly from before to after its closest approach to the Sun
fell faster on the way out than it rose on the way in
2.7 to 10 billion kg, depending on the assumed dust speed
the ratio of C₂ to CN nearly doubled between September and November 2025
no absorption that survives every calibration they tried
papers.why: It is a complete before-and-after record of material from another planetary system being heated by a star for possibly the first time in billions of years, and a benchmark for the next interstellar visitor.
papers.careful: The mass figures depend on assumed grain sizes and the size of the nucleus. The paper is submitted, not yet reviewed.

papers.t: Three subpopulations of binary black holes in mass, spin magnitudes and tilts following GWTC-5
papers.by: Asad Hussain, Maximiliano Isi and Aaron Zimmerman
papers.status: 33 pages, 23 figures
papers.one: The 259 black hole mergers detected so far seem to fall into three families, told apart by how fast the black holes spin.
papers.q: Pairs of black holes can form in more than one way: from two stars born together, or from black holes that meet in a crowded cluster, some of them products of earlier mergers. Each route should leave a mark on the masses and spins. Can the catalogue be sorted that way?
papers.how: A statistical model that lets the data divide itself into groups, each with its own pattern of mass ratio, spin and spin direction, applied to the 259 mergers in the fifth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA catalogue.
found: dominates near 35 solar masses; both holes barely spin; nearly equal masses
about half the pairs near 10 solar masses; spins about 0.2, roughly aligned with the orbit
dominates above 60 solar masses; the heavier hole spins at about 0.7, pointing in any direction
papers.why: Fast, randomly tilted spins in the heaviest pairs are what you expect if those black holes were themselves made in earlier mergers. The result adds to the evidence that the detectors are seeing more than one origin story.
papers.careful: The families come from a flexible statistical model; the abstract does not tie each to a specific formation route. Not yet peer reviewed.
